lines.text: It rains on Titan. But not water.
And what fills its lakes is even stranger. Stay for it.
Titan is Saturn's biggest moon, larger than the planet Mercury.
It's about minus one hundred seventy-nine degrees. Far too cold for liquid water.
lines.caption: It's about -179°C. Far too cold for liquid water.

lines.text: Instead, the clouds rain methane, and it carves real rivers.
Those rivers fill lakes and seas of liquid natural gas, the kind some stoves burn on Earth.
It's the only place besides Earth known to have liquid on its surface.
Sounds fake? It's true. Follow for more.
